dedupe_keys.name: uk national risk register 2025 reasonable worst case scenarios for 89 national risks

description: The National Risk Register is the public version of the UK government's National Security Risk Assessment and sets out the most serious acute risks facing the United Kingdom at national scale. The 2025 edition, published on 16 January 2025 as a 187-page PDF, covers 89 risks in nine themes (terrorism, cyber, state threats, geographic and diplomatic, accidents and systems failures, natural and environmental hazards, human, animal and plant health, societal, and conflict and instability), many of them about infrastructure, such as attacks on gas, electricity and fuel supply infrastructure, failure of gas supply and water infrastructure, financial market infrastructure and severe space weather. For each risk it gives a reasonable worst-case scenario, the worst plausible manifestation, with likelihood scored 1 to 5 over five years for non-malicious and two years for malicious risks, impact, and the capabilities needed for response and recovery, drawn from departments, devolved governments, scientists, industry and academia. It is the first edition aligned with the dynamic NSRA process and is aimed at risk and resilience practitioners, including operators of critical national infrastructure. The register is accessible as a free PDF on GOV.UK under the Open Government Licence. Caveats: chronic risks are excluded, scenarios are planning assumptions, not predictions, and the underlying modelling is not published. It supports scenario design for hazard exposure, cascading failure and emergency response simulation of infrastructure; a related record is NISMOD.
